parts.name: frame body

physics.Basic_description: Dark grey, matte-finished C-shaped metal frame forming the backbone of the clamp.
physics.Functional_description: Provides the rigid structural support to resist the clamping force generated by the screw.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the vertical spine or the top/bottom arms of the C-frame to stabilize the tool.
physics.reason: Cast iron C-clamp frames are typically solid castings to handle high compressive loads without bending.

parts.description: Dark grey, matte-finished C-shaped metal frame forming the backbone of the clamp.
parts.function: Provides the rigid structural support to resist the clamping force generated by the screw.

parts.name: anvil pad

physics.Basic_description: Small, light grey circular pad located at the tip of the fixed jaw.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a flat, hard contact surface for the workpiece against the fixed jaw.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and flush to be grasped independently; part of the jaw interface.
physics.reason: Small functional wear pad, likely a solid steel insert or rivet.

parts.description: Small, light grey circular pad located at the tip of the fixed jaw.
parts.function: Provides a flat, hard contact surface for the workpiece against the fixed jaw.

parts.name: screw core

physics.Basic_description: Light grey cylindrical threaded rod running through the center of the clamp.
physics.Functional_description: Converts rotational torque from the handle into linear clamping force.
physics.Grasped_description: Not intended for grasping; gripping the threads would damage them and is inefficient.
physics.reason: Clamp screws must be solid steel rods to withstand high tensile stress without buckling.

parts.description: Light grey cylindrical threaded rod running through the center of the clamp.
parts.function: Converts rotational torque from the handle into linear clamping force.

parts.name: screw collar

physics.Basic_description: Small ring or collar section on the screw shaft, appearing light grey/metallic.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as a stop or bearing surface to retain the screw within the frame or handle assembly.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and integral to the screw mechanism to be grasped.
physics.reason: Machined feature on a solid rod or a solid retaining ring.

parts.description: Small ring or collar section on the screw shaft, appearing light grey/metallic.
parts.function: Acts as a stop or bearing surface to retain the screw within the frame or handle assembly.

parts.name: handle hub

physics.Basic_description: Central block connecting the T-bar handle to the screw shaft, dark grey/metallic.
physics.Functional_description: Transfers torque from the T-bar handle to the screw rod.
physics.Grasped_description: Could be grasped to turn the screw if the balls are inaccessible, but less ergonomic.
physics.reason: Must be solid to transmit high torque from the handle to the screw without shearing.

parts.description: Central block connecting the T-bar handle to the screw shaft, dark grey/metallic.
parts.function: Transfers torque from the T-bar handle to the screw rod.

parts.name: tbar

physics.Basic_description: Horizontal cylindrical bar forming the cross-piece of the T-handle, light grey.
physics.Functional_description: Provides leverage arm for the user to rotate the screw.
physics.Grasped_description: Grasp the bar between the end balls to apply torque for tightening or loosening.
physics.reason: Handle bars are solid rods to prevent bending under hand force.

parts.description: Horizontal cylindrical bar forming the cross-piece of the T-handle, light grey.
parts.function: Provides leverage arm for the user to rotate the screw.

parts.name: ball 0

physics.Basic_description: Spherical knobs at the ends of the T-bar handle, appearing smooth and light grey/white.
physics.Functional_description: Provides a comfortable, non-slip grip point for the user's hands to apply torque.
physics.Grasped_description: Primary grasp target; pinch or encompass one or both balls to rotate the handle.
physics.reason: Likely solid molded plastic or wood spheres for ergonomic grip; even if hollow shells, they are small and dense enough to approximate as solid for manipulation physics.

parts.description: Spherical knobs at the ends of the T-bar handle, appearing smooth and light grey/white.
parts.function: Provides a comfortable, non-slip grip point for the user's hands to apply torque.

parts.name: swivel pad

physics.Basic_description: Circular pad at the tip of the screw, designed to swivel, light grey/metallic.
physics.Functional_description: Presses against the workpiece, swiveling to accommodate non-parallel surfaces and prevent marring.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a grasp target; it is the active contact point for clamping.
physics.reason: Solid steel component designed to bear direct compressive load against the workpiece.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
